messages:
Dev Patel: Heads up escalation: we’ve got multiple customers reporting **TypeScript SDK streaming disconnects** over the last ~48h. Pattern: SSE stream starts, delivers a few tokens, then the client throws `TypeError: terminated` / `socket hang up` / `UND_ERR_SOCKET` depending on runtime.

Can folks from DevEx take a look? @Dana Lo @Ibrahim Khan

Tickets / refs:
- SUP-9334 (customer seeing odd behavior + logs with request-ids; main complaint was retrying on 429 but they also mention stream drops)
- SUP-9321 (Python streaming “hang” but might be same proxy buffering class of issue)

I’m collecting request-ids + environment details in the ticket but wanted to flag here since it’s coming in waves.

—

Owen Phillips: Adding details from 2 support chats today (no Jira yet, will file if needed):
1) Node 18, `fetch` (built-in), behind corporate proxy (Zscaler). Stream drops after ~30–60s. They said non-streaming works.
2) Node 20, `undici`, k8s ingress (nginx). Stream drops ~10s in when tokens slow down.

Both customers say they didn’t call `AbortController.abort()`. One said they see it more when the model is slow / long prompts.

—

Dana Lo: Thx. A few quick questions for triage:
- Are they using our TS SDK streaming helper (the one that parses SSE) or doing `client.responses.stream()` raw?
- Do we have the **request-id** from gateway right before the disconnect? (Header `x-request-id` should be in response; but they may not see it if they don’t log headers)
- Are they setting any timeouts? Node fetch can have odd default behavior depending on wrappers.

Also: we should confirm whether these are **mid-stream server disconnects** vs client-side timeouts/proxy.

—

Dev Patel: For the first one (proxy): they’re using the SDK stream helper.

For the nginx ingress customer: they’re using our helper too.

Request-ids: I have 3 samples from the nginx ingress case; pasting here (sanitized):
- `req_01JMCV7X9Y0W8K7E9Q1A9P2B7K`
- `req_01JMCV8A2K4R0D4Q5M9Y7H2B1T`

They said the stream ended without a final `[DONE]` / completion event. They get an error thrown from the iterator.

—

Ibrahim Khan: :eyes: This matches what we saw in the earlier streaming edge-case notes (partial frame + abrupt close). In TS specifically, the SSE parser is less forgiving if the final frame is cut.

Two likely buckets:
1) Proxy/ingress idle timeout closes the connection (common) and the SDK surfaces a generic network error.
2) We’re not handling **partial SSE frames** / chunk boundaries correctly and treating it like a fatal parse error.

Dana — do we currently retry streaming automatically anywhere? We should not.

—

Dana Lo: We do **not** intentionally retry streaming requests, but depending on how the caller wraps it, they might be re-issuing. In the SDK, the iterator throws and exits.

We *do* have one bug I remember: if the underlying reader yields an incomplete UTF-8 chunk, our decoder path can throw and we don’t attempt to buffer + continue. That would look like a “random disconnect” even if the socket stays up.

Can support ask both customers for:
- Node version
- Whether they’re on `@redwood-inference/sdk` version X (exact)
- Whether they’re using Next.js / Vercel (edge runtime does weird things)
- If behind nginx: what is `proxy_read_timeout` / `proxy_send_timeout`

Workaround we can suggest today: set ingress `proxy_read_timeout` >= 300s and disable proxy buffering for SSE (`proxy_buffering off;`).

—

Owen Phillips: For the nginx one they shared config snippet:
```
proxy_read_timeout 60s;
proxy_send_timeout 60s;
proxy_buffering on;
```
So yeah, that’s probably killing long-ish generations.

For the Zscaler one: they can’t change proxy settings.

—

Rafael Mendes: From SRE POV: even if infra kills it, SDK should:
- surface a **clear error type** (distinguish timeout vs disconnect vs cancel)
- include last seen `x-request-id` when available
- avoid any automatic retry of streams (can cause duplicate tokens/side effects)

If we add a client-side keepalive/heartbeat, it has to be on the server side (comments or ping events) to keep proxies from idling out. Otherwise customers need proxy config.

—

Sabrina James: For docs/examples, we should add a “Streaming behind proxies / load balancers” section with the nginx directives + note about Zscaler/Cloudflare.

Also we should be explicit: for streaming, set a longer overall timeout (or none) but still have connect timeout.

—

Nikhil Sharma: Can we confirm if gateway is sending any periodic data for long tool calls / long thinking? If we can’t, customers behind 60s idle proxies will keep seeing this.

—

Dana Lo: Gateway currently only sends tokens as they’re produced; if the model stalls (tool call, long prompt processing), there can be a long gap.

We can do two parallel things:
1) SDK: harden parser for partial frames and improve error mapping.
2) Docs + support guidance: nginx settings and proxy expectations.

I’ll open an internal issue under the parity audit workstream and link PR once up (this aligns with the streaming standard work).

—

Dev Patel: :+1: For immediate support response, I’ll reply to customers with:
- nginx config guidance (`proxy_buffering off`, `proxy_read_timeout 300s`)
- ask for exact SDK + Node versions
- confirm they should not wrap streaming call with generic retry logic

Also filing new Jira tickets for the TS streaming cases so we can track volume separately from SUP-9334.

—

SupportBot: Reminder: Please add customer-visible impact + workaround to Jira tickets and tag component `sdk-typescript` + label `streaming`.

—

Ibrahim Khan: One more ask: can we get raw logs from the TS SDK with debug enabled? If we don’t have that today, we should add a quick snippet for support to send.

Something like “enable client debug and capture last 50 lines + request-id”.

—

Owen Phillips: I can draft the snippet for customers. For Node we can suggest:
- set `REDWOOD_LOG=debug` (if supported) or pass a logger
- log response headers on stream start

But I don’t think TS SDK has a standardized env var yet.

—

Dana Lo: Yeah, TS logging is inconsistent. For now, ask them to wrap with their own logging and capture:
- response status + headers
- the thrown error object (including `cause`)

We’ll fix “how to enable debug logging” as part of the parity effort.

—

Dev Patel: Closing loop: I’ll keep this thread updated as more tickets come in + once we have confirmation whether it’s mostly proxy idle timeout vs parser bug.

Current hypothesis split:
- nginx customers: mostly infra timeout/buffering
- Zscaler customers: likely unavoidable unless server sends periodic events OR we provide non-streaming fallback guidance

Thanks all.
